items: 500g leeks (about 3 large), trimmed, washed and sliced
1/4 - 1/2 tsp of freshly grated nutmeg (or 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg)
1 jar white beans - with their liquid (Bold Bean’s are best)
Warm, crusty bread and butter - to serve (I love a toasted, dense, dark rye bread - this one is my favourite)

steps: Heat a few tablespoons of olive oil in a heavy-based saucepan over a medium heat. Add the leeks with a pinch of salt and cook gently for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and starting to sweeten, but not coloured. Take care not to brown or burn them - a gentle steam under a lid will help to bring out their natural sweetness without the bitterness.
Add the parsnips and garlic and cook for a further 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the parsnips are lightly coloured.

Stir in the nutmeg, then pour in about 500ml of the stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 12-15 minutes, or until the parsnips are completely tender. Depending on your pan and how thick or loose you like your soup, you might want to add a little extra stock as you go - it’s easier to thin than to thicken!
Add the white beans and their liquid, give everything a stir and cook for another 2 minutes to warm the beans through - if you’re using canned beans, you may need a little more stock.

Using a hand blender, blitz the soup until smooth and creamy, adding more stock or water if needed to reach your desired consistency. Taste and season with salt, cracked black pepper and a bit more nutmeg too, if you like.
Ladle the soup into bowls, finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve alongside a nicely buttered bit of warm, crusty bread.
